title: ReadonlyArray, ReadonlySet, and immutable views
hook: readonly T[] and ReadonlyArray<T> block mutating methods at compile time — but the underlying array is still mutable at runtime if another reference exists. Immutable views protect callers without copying data.

blocks.text: **readonly T[]** (or **ReadonlyArray<T>**) removes mutating methods like `push`, `pop`, and `splice` from the type and makes index assignment an error. **ReadonlySet<T>** and **ReadonlyMap<K,V>** are interfaces describing read-only views. **Readonly<T>** is a mapped type that recursively marks properties readonly. At runtime, `readonly` does nothing — it is purely a compile-time contract. Deep immutability requires recursive Readonly or libraries like Immer.

entries.plainDefinition: Array type without mutating methods — index assignment blocked at compile time.
Interface equivalent of readonly T[] — same semantics.
readonly on container — nested objects remain mutable.
Utility making all properties readonly recursively one level.

blocks.text: Function parameters that should not mutate input should use `readonly T[]` — signals intent and prevents accidental `push`. React props are readonly. Redux state snapshots use readonly types. C# has `IReadOnlyList<T>` with runtime enforcement on the wrapper; TypeScript readonly is erased — a malicious caller can still cast away readonly. Senior interviews probe shallow vs deep immutability and when to use `Readonly<T>` vs `readonly` modifier on arrays.

blocks.title: Covariance note
blocks.body: readonly arrays are covariant in element type — readonly Animal[] accepts readonly Dog[]. Mutable T[] is invariant.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Parameter types
items.body: Accept readonly T[] when function only reads — wider assignability from mutable arrays.

items.title: Return views
items.body: Return readonly slice results without copying — caller cannot mutate via return type.

items.title: Readonly<T> on objects
items.body: Props interfaces and DTO views — one level deep by default.

items.title: Deep freeze at runtime
items.body: Object.freeze for runtime — combine with readonly for compile-time.

snippet.label: readonly parameter accepts mutable array
snippet.explanation: readonly parameter is bivariant for acceptance — mutable arrays pass in. Mutations blocked on the readonly view inside the function.

snippet.label: Shallow readonly trap
snippet.explanation: readonly Row[] only prevents reassignment of rows array — cells inside each Row remain mutable. Use Readonly<Row> or deep readonly for nested safety.

snippet.label: ReadonlySet and ReadonlyMap views
snippet.explanation: ReadonlyMap is a typing view — underlying Map still mutable via original reference. Interface omits mutating methods.

snippet.label: Failure mode — cast away readonly
snippet.explanation: readonly is not enforced at runtime. Cast to mutable type allows mutation. Use Object.freeze in security-sensitive paths.

blocks.title: Assuming runtime immutability
blocks.body: readonly is compile-time only — cast or shared reference can still mutate.

blocks.title: Shallow readonly on nested data
blocks.body: readonly on outer array does not freeze inner objects — use deep Readonly or validation.

blocks.text: readonly T[] enables covariant element types — important for function parameter typing. `ReadonlyArray` vs `readonly T[]` are identical in modern TS. For React 19+ and signals, readonly props prevent accidental state mutation in child components. Immer produces mutable drafts with readonly snapshots. In performance-critical code, readonly views avoid array copy while documenting intent — copy only when true isolation needed.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Claiming readonly freezes at runtime. Not knowing shallow vs deep. Unaware readonly arrays are covariant.

interviewTakeaways: readonly T[] blocks push/pop/splice — compile-time only.
Mutable arrays assignable to readonly parameters — covariant.
Shallow readonly — nested objects still mutable.
60s: Use readonly on params and return views to signal no mutation. Not runtime safe — cast bypasses. Deep immutability needs recursive Readonly or Immer.
Follow-up: Readonly<T> mapped type, IReadOnlyList in C#.
commonPitfalls: Weak: "readonly makes array immutable at runtime" — rejected.
Expecting nested immutability from readonly outer array.
Strong: "readonly is erased at emit. Shallow view only. Use deep types or freeze for nested safety."

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS Object.freeze provides shallow runtime immutability; TS readonly is compile-time only with no runtime cost.
C# IReadOnlyList<T> wraps with runtime mutation guards; TS readonly is a type-system contract erased on emit.
